Q: How do I convert a password into asterisks while it is being entered? A:

I created a cross-platform Python library inspired by pwinput, but with more features, allowing you to ignore special keys (such as arrows keys, escape, F1-F12, etc.), working from Python version 3.9 to the current version.

To install it:

pip install masked-input

And for basic usage:

from masked_input import masked_input

# Basic usage with default settings
password = masked_input()  # Displays "Password: " with "•" masking

If you need more information, I invite you to take a look at:

  • https://pypi.org/project/masked-input

  • https://github.com/ree-verse/masked-input

Q: How can I estimate or count input tokens for a PDF before sending it to AWS Bedrock, since CountTokens API doesn't support document input? A:

Sounds like this could have been a real (Q&A) question, not an open-ended question. You are not really asking about best practices or opinions.

Take

  1. What is the recommended way to estimate or pre-calculate how many tokens a PDF will consume before sending it to Bedrock?
  2. Are there better architectural approaches to guard against excessive token usage?

and rephrase to:

How can you estimate or pre-calculate how many tokens a PDF will consume before sending it to Bedrock?

voilà, a perfectly answerable, objective question.

Q: How to clear search highlights with <Esc> in Vim? A:

I have this in my vimrc and it has worked perfectly:

set hlsearch

" Clear highlights.
" We need this noop mapping before, otherwise
" the esc mapping will just *completely* break.
nnoremap <Esc>\ <Esc>\
nnoremap <nowait> <silent> <Esc> <Esc>:noh<CR>

" Removes delay from closing fzf search popup.
tnoremap <Esc>\ <Esc>\
tnoremap <nowait> <silent> <Esc> <Esc>

Can't remember all the nuances in originally constructing it like this.

Q: flutter version need set up in fvm A:

Although my question received many downvotes, I think it’s still worth writing an answer. Who knows maybe it will help others.

First, open a terminal (bash / PowerShell) and run:

where fvm

I discovered that FVM was installed via Chocolatey. Because of that, running:

dart pub global activate fvm had no effect.

To fix this, uninstall FVM from Chocolatey:

choco uninstall fvm

After uninstalling, run again:

fvm --version

Now it should show the latest FVM version installed via dart pub.

Finally, you can run:

fvm list

It should correctly display the installed Flutter versions without showing the “need setup” issue.
